quotes.text: Learn how to use Checkout to collect payments on your website.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Checkout is a low-code payment integration that creates a customizable form for collecting payments.
When customers are ready to complete their purchase, your application creates a new `Checkout Session`.
these payment methods don’t appear for return purchases in Checkout.
By default, a `Checkout Session` expires after 24 hours.

findings: New raw lines 5-16 supply only the Checkout subject and four variant links: Full hosted page, Full embedded page, Embedded form, and Elements. Old raw lines 8-371 carry actual Hosted page, Embedded page and Checkout elements bodies. The November capture establishes navigation/taxonomy, not changed runtime behavior or deprecation of April details.

Navigation changed materially for routing: old raw lines 14-16,190-192,350-352 used stripe-hosted, embedded-form, checkout-elements variant identifiers; new raw lines 13-16 use stripe-hosted, embedded-page, checkout-form, checkout-elements. The new Embedded form target has no pinned body; do not equate it automatically with the old embedded-form variant merely because of the label. Current source line 24 calls this 'all 3 UI modes' without date or index qualification, so distinguish three old full bodies from four new navigation targets.

Current source lines 4-18 and 150-163 contain 12 older raw files but not the new index. Add November provenance without removing those other distinct raw sources; do not treat address/name/consent/quantity facts from separate raw files as claims in the new 16-line capture.

Old raw lines 22-25,73-91 show hosted flow: server creates Checkout Session with payment mode, line items and success_url, sends customer to session.url, then handles completion via event destination/webhook. Old raw lines 198-202,243-263 show embedded_page and return_url instead of hosted session.url; old raw lines 350-363 show Checkout Elements on-site form. Current source lines 67-80 summarizes these but 'customer pays' and fulfillment on checkout.session.completed need a delayed-payment/status qualification, as related concept wiki/concepts/stripe-checkout.md lines 200-216 already states.

Old raw lines 94-108 and 265-279 distinguish payment mode one-time purchases from subscription mode recurring and mixed carts; line_items can mix recurring and one-time Prices in subscription mode. Old raw lines 135-153 and 307-325 distinguish payment-mode payment_intent_data.setup_future_usage, subscription default saving, customer-configured Account versus Customer default-payment-method fields and guest customers. Accounts v2 preview/version caveat at old raw lines 143-161 remains dated, not current account eligibility.

Old raw lines 163-176 and 335-348 state Session 24-hour default expiry, expires_at 30 minutes to 24 hours, explicit expiration, and webhook processing for completion versus expiry. Current source line 31 says checkout.session.expired 'fires to release inventory', whereas old raw line 176 says the application processes the event to return items; automatic inventory release should not be inferred.

The old Hosted feature table at old raw lines 36-63 has 11 built-in rows and 15 customizable rows (26 total), not 24; current source lines 24,28-29 calls it a 24-feature list/11 plus 13. Current source lines 39-65 further combines card validation and error messaging into one row. The reciprocal retrieval routes also repeat the wrong count: wiki/concepts/stripe-checkout.md line 252 and coordinator-owned wiki/stripe-index.md line 34 both call this source a '24-feature table'. Correct the dated April Hosted table to 26 rows or omit counts in the source, concept route and Stripe-index label; keep card validation and error messaging as separate built-in rows and hosted-only custom domains at old raw lines 43-44,54,69-71. This is a baseline summary/route error, not a November raw change.

Related concept wiki/concepts/stripe-checkout.md lines 12-32 uses its own earlier two-option/three-hosting-mode taxonomy and later lines 44-60 date the Stripe.js v9 Checkout Form beta. The new navigation route checkout-form alone does not establish the same SDK contract or general availability; any concept route should remain version-aware.
historical_claims_to_preserve: 2026-04-20 old raw lines 8-12: Checkout as a low-code website payment form with hosted, embedded and Elements integration families; >100 payment methods and one-time/subscription support are dated page claims.

2026-04-20 old raw lines 14-25,73-91,190-202,243-263,350-363: three captured UI bodies and their distinct hosted session.url/success_url, embedded_page/return_url and Checkout Elements paths; the November index labels do not substitute for their bodies.

conflicts: Current source lines 24,28-29 say 24 features, 11 built-in and 13 customizable, and wiki/concepts/stripe-checkout.md line 252 plus coordinator-owned wiki/stripe-index.md line 34 repeat a '24-feature table' route label. Current source lines 71-80 show 'customer pays' followed by checkout.session.completed fulfillment; related concept lines 200-216 warns that Session completion can precede asynchronous payment success. Make fulfillment conditional on paid status or async success for paid orders.
Current source line 31 describes checkout.session.expired as releasing inventory; old raw line 176 assigns inventory return to the application's event handler.

Old raw lines 190-192 call the embedded variant embedded-form but the example uses ui_mode embedded_page at lines 252-263; new raw lines 14-15 splits embedded-page and checkout-form navigation. The pinned record does not resolve behavioral equivalence among these labels.

source_assessments.reason: The raw delta is navigation and route taxonomy only, but the current summary needs distinct November provenance, corrected old-table counts and important Checkout state/outcome qualifications.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/how-checkout-works, new raw lines 5-16 establish the website-payment topic and four variant routes, with no captured variant instructions. Old raw lines 8-25,73-108,135-176,190-202,243-279 and 350-363 document three April 2026 bodies: hosted Session URL with success_url, embedded_page with return_url, and on-site Checkout Elements; payment versus subscription/mixed-cart mode, Account or Customer versus guest identity, saving choices, expiry and webhook handling are separate boundaries. source-stripe-how-checkout-works.md maps these earlier flows and other historical raw files, but its three-mode framing needs a November navigation qualification and its completion/fulfillment wording must not imply payment success for delayed methods.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/how-checkout-works, new raw lines 9-16 are navigation and presentation: four named links, including embedded-page and checkout-form, compared with old raw lines 14-16,190-192 and 350-352 three full variant bodies. source-stripe-how-checkout-works.md should retain the April 2026 feature, Session, mode, identity, expiration and agentic claims as dated history and add the November index separately. Its 24-feature/13-customizable count conflicts with old raw lines 36-63, which has 11 built-in and 15 customizable rows (26 total), including separate card-validation and error-messaging rows at old raw lines 43-44. The same false '24-feature table' label appears in wiki/concepts/stripe-checkout.md line 252 and coordinator-owned wiki/stripe-index.md line 34; all three retrieval routes need the dated 26-row count or no count. This is an older baseline summary error, not a November raw change. A Session creation, return_url or checkout.session.completed event does not itself prove paid status; paid orders with delayed methods require status or asynchronous-success handling. Expiry events enable merchant inventory action, and uncaptured linked bodies cannot establish Checkout Form behavior or current SDK support.
